overview: This Senate resolution honors the 17 students and teachers killed in the February 14, 2018, mass shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida, marking seven years since the attack. It offers condolences to the victims' families and friends, honors the survivors and pledges continued support for their recovery, and recognizes the strength of the school community. It also thanks the emergency medical and health care workers who responded and cared for the victims and survivors. The resolution does not change any law or spending. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on February 13, 2025.
for: Supporters say marking the anniversary keeps the victims' memory alive and shows the Parkland community and survivors that the nation has not forgotten them.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and changes no law or spending, and offers remembrance without any policy steps to prevent similar attacks.
